name: Street photography
summary: Unposed pictures of public life, made with a small camera, a wide lens and quick reflexes. The photographer finds the frame and waits for the moment when gesture, light and geometry agree.

philosophy.core_thesis: Public life holds pictures that nobody can stage, and the photographer's job is to be in the right place and to see them in time.
design_principles: Use a 28mm or 35mm lens (35mm format) and stand 1 to 3m from the subject, so that context and person share the frame.
Zone-focus at f/8 to f/11 on a set distance of 2 to 3m, and keep the shutter at 1/250s or faster.
Shoot in found light: hard sun and deep shadow at a ratio of 8:1 or more, or the mixed light of a street at night.
Layer the frame: put at least three planes (foreground, subject, background) in it, and let edges and shadows cut figures.
Wait for the gesture: release when the hand, the gaze or the step is at its peak, within a 1/250s window.
Print with a hard grade: true black, bright highlights and visible grain.
anti_patterns: Posed subjects who look at the lens and smile
Shallow depth of field that isolates a single face from the street
Telephoto compression from a hidden distance
Heavy retouching, cloning or removal of distracting people
Flat, even light with no shadow geometry
Staged scenes with props or hired models

composition.framing: Tight and often tilted; the edges cut figures on purpose, and the frame is full.
composition.viewpoint: Eye or chest height, handheld, 1 to 3m from the subject.
composition.geometry: Diagonals, shadows and doorways make a stage; several small events share one frame.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre, in a pocket of light or against a clean wall, with a second figure or sign in balance.

principles.rule: Cut figures at the frame edge with a margin of 0–5%, so that the edge is part of the picture.
Put 3 planes in the frame: foreground at 1–2m, subject at 2–4m and background beyond 6m.
Give 1 primary gesture and 0 to 2 secondary ones; release at the peak, within 1/250s.
Hold a shadow-to-sun difference of 5 stops or more.
Put the main figure within 0.05 of 0.33 or 0.67 of the width.

light.quality: Found light: hard direct sun or the mixed lights of the night street.
light.direction: Low side light and backlight give long shadows and rim light.
light.time_of_day: Early morning or late afternoon, when shadows are long

lens_and_camera.format: 35mm rangefinder or compact SLR; digital full frame as a modern equivalent
lens_and_camera.aperture: f/8 to f/11 (f/2 only at night)
lens_and_camera.focus: Zone focus: set the distance to 2–3m at f/8 and do not refocus; the depth of field covers 1.5 to 6m.

colour_and_grade.treatment: High-contrast black and white with a strong grain, or restrained colour that keeps the tone of the scene.
grade_recipe: Convert to monochrome with a yellow-orange filter mix (R 50, G 50, B 0).
Set the black point at 1% and the white point at 98%.
Apply +30% midtone contrast with a steep S-curve.
Burn the corners by −0.5 stop and dodge the face by +0.3 stop.
Add film grain, amount 25%, size 40%, as for Tri-X pushed one stop.
Keep the full frame; crop by no more than 5%.
colour_and_grade.grain: Tri-X 400 at EI 800: coarse and visible at A4

subject_and_staging.staging: None. The photographer picks a place with good light and waits, or walks and reacts.
subject_and_staging.direction: Nobody is asked to pose; subjects are unaware of the camera or ignore it.

workflow: Develop in a standard developer; push by one stop when the light is low.
Make a work print of every frame on a contact sheet and mark the best moment.
Print on grade 3 to 4 paper with burning at the edges.
Keep the black frame edge visible to show the full frame.
post_processing.output: A grainy, high-contrast 8×10 in print, or a 4:5 digital file with the frame edge visible.

emotion.target_response: Alertness and recognition: the viewer feels a moment that was nearly missed and is real.

use_cases: campaign imagery with a raw feel
avoid_when: The brief needs a controlled product shot or a clean studio portrait.
The subject cannot appear in public, for reasons of consent or law.

modifiers.how: Move to a tripod and a view camera, stop down to f/32, and wait for the light; keep the black and white and the strong tonal range.
Switch to colour slide film at ISO 64, f/8, 1/250s, and keep the found subject and the low angle; make colour the subject.

sources.title: Henri Cartier-Bresson, The Decisive Moment (Simon & Schuster, 1952)
Colin Westerbeck and Joel Meyerowitz, Bystander: A History of Street Photography (Bulfinch, 1994)
